text:
toni_sales: Quick heads-up — TidalWave wants a performance validation for their checkout conversational flow. Key asks: sustain 275 qps, tolerate short microbursts to 800 qps (15-25s), and keep p95 < 190ms. They want a 1-page runbook, a short slide with results, and hosted vs dedicated cost delta.
sam_se: Got it. Do we have their representative prompt set and token averages? that's needed for batching/throughput math.
yara_perf: They shared a sample: median prompt ~58 tokens, median response ~150 tokens => ~208 tokens per request avg. Model: community 70B quant-8 variant. Traffic mix: ~60% short chat, 40% long completions.
sam_se: Proposed test phases: 1) warmup 5m at 30% target qps; 2) steady-state 45m at 275 qps (longer to show thermal stability); 3) burst matrix (5 bursts: 500, 650, 800, 800, 600 qps; 20s each, 90s apart); 4) cross-AZ fallback trial (10% traffic -> fallback region for 12m). Add cooldown steps.
toni_sales: Include prewarm guidance — they highlighted cold-start tails as a key worry.
yara_perf: Prewarm plan: a) push 2k representative prefixes to prime KV cache; b) run a 10m low-concurrency fill to warm kernels and allocator; c) keep 10% warm standby for Dedicated or 2 warm workers on Hosted during demo. Also capture a KV-empty vs KV-primed sweep.
miles_ops: Sizing notes: with quant-8 and our runtime optimizations, sustained 275 qps is ~5 A100-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and KV. To safely absorb 800 qps microbursts keep ~9 GPUs or rely on autoscale with 75-90s cooldown. Hosted expected unit-cost ~1.7-1.9x vs Dedicated for same peak.
sam_se: Measurement matrix: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, avg batch size distribution, GPU utilization, queue length over time, and sampled traces (1% sampling) for root-cause. Also capture inter-region RTT during fallback trial.
clara_sec: Security checklist flagged by TidalWave: SAML SSO, customer KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained 90d, and encryption in transit+at-rest confirmations. If we use any production PII they require signed DPA and KMS key exchange; demo corpus ok on Hosted.
toni_sales: Quick pricing ask: rough monthly ballpark for 1.2M requests/month at ~208 tokens/request — exec wants a number to compare Hosted vs small Dedicated commit.
miles_ops: Quick ballpark: Hosted inference-only ~= $4.6k/mo (token billing and burst charges vary). Small Dedicated reserved amortized ~= $2.9k/mo plus ops/support. We'll refine the appendix after runs.
yara_perf: Load generator snippet we'll use (wrk2 + lua mix):
```
wrk -t12 -c360 -d20s -R800 --script=dialog_mix.lua --latency $TARGET_HOST
```
Steady-state run uses -R275 for 45m. Include our x-rw-trace header for token accounting and token/sec metrics.
build-bot: CI job #8890 completed: loadgen image build OK, scripts uploaded.
yara_perf: Dry-run quick summary: warmup OK. Steady 275 qps -> p95 ~185ms, p99 ~405ms. 800 qps bursts (20s) -> p95 spiked to ~510ms, p99 ~1.15s. With KV-cache disabled steady p95 increased ~32%. GPU util avg ~83% during sustained, spikes to 99% during bursts. Raw logs and CSVs in secure storage link.
sam_se: Those look solid. Follow-ups: 1) run a KV-disabled sweep and quantify delta (yara). 2) run a low-batch-wait (512ms) sweep to show latency improvement tradeoff.
clara_sec: Reminder: before any run with their production data we need DPA signed + SSO test account + KMS exchange. I'll share the exact clause and a short security appendix.
toni_sales: Action items: a) I'll confirm DPA path and upload final corpus (EOD today). b) miles will confirm test cluster snapshot and autoscale policy (done by 07:30 PT tomorrow). c) yara runs dry-run and posts results + one-pager. d) clara prepares security appendix and required artifacts.
miles_ops: Test cluster provisioned: 9 x A10g-equivalent in us-west2, logs to ephemeral secure bucket, autoscaler set with 75s cooldown; creds in vault.
yara_perf: I'll assemble the one-pager + 3-slide deck (p95/p99 charts, GPU util heatmap, batch distribution, recommended runtime knobs, and cost appendix).
build-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance Sat 02:00-04:00 PT — avoid scheduling runs then.
toni_sales: Thanks team — I'll sync with TidalWave and propose Friday 10:00 PT for the customer-facing run. :thumbsup:
